provider: 1fichier — registered free account, 5 TB of temporary storage with FTP + API

free_tier.stated: 5 TB of temporary storage on a free account.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: The help page states the 300 GB file-size cap applies to every plan, with an unlimited file count on every plan.

retention.stated: the file is removed 30 days after it was uploaded, or 90 days after its last qualified access.
retention.notes: The help page states 15 days without an account, 30 days on a free account, the whole subscription period on a paid plan; a qualified access extends a free file to 90 days.

egress.terms: Downloads are unlimited on the free tier but ad/wait-gated and speed-limited, with a human-verification step; Premium removes ads and gives 300 GB per file and unlimited speed. Free-tier egress is 'unmetered but shaped'. The shaping, not the bytes, is the limit.

tooling: Documented REST API, open to every registered account; download tokens and FTP sub-accounts are reserved to paid plans, and requests are limited to 3 per second. FTP upload and remote upload (URL pull) on free accounts. rclone ships a 1fichier backend, whose documentation says a Premium subscription is required to use it.
chaining: Free accounts need only an email address, so the up-to-5 TB of temporary storage is per account; every file still expires 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access.

limits.value: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access

limits_note: Files expire 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access. Up to 300 GB per file per the help page; web upload 500 files and 500 GB per upload, 4 hours maximum. The 5 TB is 'temporary storage'.

identity_cost.detail: registration asks for an email address, a password and a confirmation code

reliability_note: 1fichier/DStorage is a carrier with its own transit, so egress is not a marginal cost for them. Which is why the free 5 TB survives where others died. The 30/90-day retention clock is the practical failure mode: it is a staging area, not an archive.

extras.document_section: File hosts with a protocol endpoint
extras.verified_at_basis: the seed research pass, which ended 2026-10-21; this record was not re-checked against the live service
extras.quota_verbatim: Registered (free) tier: '5 TB of temporary storage', folder sharing, remote upload, FTP upload, and API access. Paid ladder: Premium Light 500 GB €10/yr, 1000 GB €20/yr, Premium €54/yr with 4 TB cold storage, Premium GOLD €108/yr with 10 TB.
extras.limits_verbatim: Retention is the killer, quoted: 'Retention: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access'. Per-file cap on free tier is not 300 GB (that is Premium Light); free-tier file size is lower and undocumented on this page — unverified. 5 TB is 'temporary storage', not durable.
extras.egress_verbatim: Downloads are unlimited on the free tier but ad/wait-gated and speed-limited, with a human-verification step; Premium removes ads and gives 300 GB per file and unlimited speed. Free-tier egress is 'unmetered but shaped' — the shaping, not the bytes, is the limit.
extras.chaining_verbatim: The multiplier is real and already known to the corpus: free accounts are email-only, and 5 TB per account is the largest genuinely-free quota found in this slot. Cross-referenced against dossier A (1fichier already appears there as 'free registered account (FTP + REST API)').
extras.tooling_verbatim: Documented public API plus FTP upload and remote upload (URL pull). rclone has no native 1fichier backend, so this is wrapper/API territory — the API is the client.
extras.agent_focus: VPS/hosting communities — NodeSeek, Hostloc, LowEndTalk, LowEndSpirit, r/selfhosted, r/DataHoarder, WebHostingTalk — for free/trial storage VPS, the large-capacity VPS culture, and the economics of excess use

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
